subject: Top-up options: voucher vs temporary capacity (BrightByte mid-cycle growth)
messages:

Cc: ops@brightbyte.com
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Need quick guidance — mid-cycle capacity bump (voucher vs top-up)

Hi Sofia,

Quick note from our side — traffic for our recommendation engine spiked unexpectedly after a product change. We need an interim capacity increase of roughly 400M tokens/month for the next 2–3 months, then expect to normalize.

Can you advise whether we should: 
- purchase a short-term voucher (3 months) at the listed uplift rate, or
- do a top-up bucket billed pro-rata on next invoice, or
- add temporary dedicated capacity with a mid-cycle true-up at renewal?

Key constraints: minimal procurement friction, want to avoid long-term price premium if possible, and ideally co-term with our annual renewal in January. Finance prefers a single PO if feasible.

Appreciate a quick high-level recommendation and any ballpark costs.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform
BrightByte

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Need quick guidance — mid-cycle capacity bump (voucher vs top-up)

Hi Elena — thanks for the context, and sorry about the spike. I copied Ben (sales) and Tessa (billing) so we can triage procurement and timing.

Short answer: recommend a hybrid approach to minimize friction and cost risk. High-level options:

1) 3-month voucher (fastest)
   - Pros: single PO, immediate capacity, minimal legal/procurement.
   - Cons: premium per-token rate (~+18%) and risk of stranded capacity if usage drops fast.

2) Pro-rata top-up bucket (invoice line item)
   - Pros: lowest per-token marginal cost, aligns with monthly billing, flexible.
   - Cons: requires billing team to accept mid-cycle change; may need a short PO or amended invoice process.

3) Temporary dedicated capacity with co-term true-up (6+ months recommended)
   - Pros: predictable SLOs, lower unit cost during commitment period; we can true-up/annualize at January renewal for blended pricing.
   - Cons: procurement heavier, longer commitment window.

My recommendation: offer a 3-month voucher to get them through the immediate spike, plus an option to convert any unused voucher tokens into a bridging credit applied toward a 6-month temporary capacity commit that co-terms to January. That gives BrightByte minimal procurement friction now and a path to smoother economics at renewal.

I attached a quick estimate (BrightByte_topup_estimate_v1.xlsx) with ballpark numbers for the three approaches — see the high-level summary in the first tab. If that sounds acceptable, Ben can draft a short amendment and Tessa can confirm invoice flow.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call today at 3pm PT to walk through numbers?

Best,
Sofia

Sofia / Tessa — quick internal note before the 3pm call.

Numbers (ballpark):
- 400M tokens/month x 3 months via voucher = $18,000/month equivalent at voucher rate (effective +18% uplift) -> total ~$54k
- Pro-rata top-up (no commitment) = $46k total over 3 months (lower unit cost)
- Temporary 6-month commit (co-term to Jan true-up) with 10% transitional discount = $82k over 6 months (effective monthly lower than voucher once annualized)

Commercial suggestion: offer the voucher for immediate relief but include a convert-to-commit option with a 10% incentive if they convert within 60 days. That preserves our ability to sell them into a longer commit while respecting BrightByte's ask for low procurement friction.

Operational asks:
- Tessa: confirm we can 1) accept a 3-month voucher PO and 2) issue a credit path if they elect conversion.
- Sofia: get buy-in from Elena on the convert option during the call.

If Tessa confirms the credit path, I think we can sign off.

Ben
